LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: HANDWRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing 3.1 Guided writing: Arabic Alphabet (2 sessions) • Symbols/Characters of
Topic 3.2: Guided writing: Handwriting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided writing: Handwriting, part of Writing 3.1 Guided writing: Arabic Alphabet (2 sessions) • Symbols/Characters of in Grade 4 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How can you develop a good handwriting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. collaborate with peers to discuss the characteristics of a good handwriting,

2. trace letters neatly and legibly with appropriate spacing and accuracy,

3. copy simple words on the names of family members neatly and legibly,

4. display their neatly written words in the language corner for peer review,

5. participate in a writing contest on handwriting and neat presentation of written works.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. collaborate with peers to discuss the characteristics of a good handwriting,
2. trace letters neatly and legibly with appropriate spacing and accuracy,
3. copy simple words on the names of family members neatly and legibly,
4. display their neatly written words in the language corner for peer review,
5. participate in a writing contest on handwriting and neat presentation of written works.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided writing: Handwriting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving: This is enhanced as the learner collaborates with peers using facts and examples to

discuss the characteristics of a good handwriting.

Values:
Integrity: This is promoted as learner exhibits transparency when displaying their neatly written words in the language corner for

peer review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is promoted as the learner accommodates and show kindness to each other as they work in groups to

accomplish tasks.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to link the concept of good handwriting to their learning of similar concepts in English and Kiswahili.
